page: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd5 is a bare metal server configured with an AMD EPYC 9255 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier performance in several areas. The server achieves top 10% placement in Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics, stress-ng single-core CPU performance, and PassMark memory scores. Software compilation with Clang, image processing, and text processing also rank in the top 10%. Multi-core stress-ng performance, PassMark CPU scores, and database operations fall into the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show strong read-only performance in the top 25% for both small and large blocks, though large block write bandwidth is average, placing in the middle 50%.

With its high memory-to-core ratio and dedicated bare metal resources, this server provides high resource density for memory-intensive workloads. It demonstrates strong capabilities for static web serving and small-model LLM inference, where prompt processing and text generation for 135M models rank in the top 10%. However, processing larger models like the 7B parameter model results in average prompt processing speeds. The hardware profile is suited for database operations, software compilation, memory-cached applications, and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without virtualization overhead.
